answer: FINN's valuation rule divides the P/E by yearly profit growth to assess if a valuation is high. HDFC Bank has a P/E of 13.5 and a profit growth rate of 7.9%, giving a valuation of 1.7x, which FINN's scorecard reads as Fair.

figures.text: Price to earnings (P/E): 13.5
Profit growth FINN's valuation uses (last year's profit growth): 7.9%
P/E over that growth: 1.7x, which FINN's scorecard reads as Fair

Valuation rule: FINN divides the P/E by yearly profit growth (in %): 1x or less reads cheap for its growth, up to 2x fair, above 2x rich. It uses 3-year growth, or last year's when one year in three grew 40% or more and last year grew less than half the 3-year rate. If PAT fell 20% or more YoY in the latest quarter, growth is in doubt.
